premise: After my husband died, I used his $85,000 life insurance to pay off my sister‑in‑law’s $82,000 tax lien on her family apple orchard, signing for 20% of cider sales and a life estate in the farmhouse, but she transferred the orchard to her daughter, forged a release, and evicted me; I found a voicemail where she admitted the debt, sued for fraud, and when she couldn’t pay the $225,000 judgment I foreclosed on the orchard and now run ‘Orchard of Omission’ cider, with every bottle of ‘Lien-Apple Cider’ stamped with the case number and a portrait of her labeled ‘Original Forger.’
